            - the invocation forms: \`/monitor @<session>\`, \`/monitor <host>:<session>\`, \`/monitor list\`
            - THE FOUR STATES and why each needs a DIFFERENT answer: QUESTION needs judgement so it goes
              to a human, STALLED is mechanical so it gets a mechanical nudge, BLOCKED must NEVER be
              nudged because that is manufactured thrash not persistence, WORKING means say nothing.
            - the two layers: the cheap 60s watcher, and the deep audit team on a slower cadence.
            - that the audit dimensions come from the WATCHED PROJECT's own rules, never a generic
              checklist, because a generic audit finds generic nothing.
            - that an audit returning "all clean" every time is an audit nobody reads, so auditors are
              adversarial and state plainly in one line when a rule genuinely holds.
            - the nudge bound: it bounds the ABSENCE OF PROGRESS, not the work, and resets on every
              advance of the build's own progress metric.
            - the seven defects as a "why the matching is so specific" section, briefly.
            - host coordinates come from ~/.ssh/config, never hardcoded.

          The frontmatter description is what makes the skill fire, so make its triggers precise and
          include both English and French phrasings, matching how sibling skills write theirs.`,
            },
            {
              key: 'rule',
              label: 'R-MONITOR rule',
              prompt: `${COMMON}

          YOUR SCOPE (only this file):
            - ${REPO}/crates/omega-core/src/rules.rs

          Add ONE new rule, R-MONITOR, so this doctrine is never re-derived. Read the R-STREAM rule in
          that file FIRST (around line 499) and match its structure, its density and its voice EXACTLY:
          R-STREAM states the canonical command, then enumerates the numbered constraints, each one
          naming the failure that taught it. R-MONITOR is its sibling: R-STREAM is "mirror a session so
          a human can watch it", R-MONITOR is "audit a session in depth, continuously, without a human".

          R-MONITOR must encode, in that same voice:
            1. The canonical command \`omega monitor <session> | <host>:<session> | list\`, and that
               watching a build NEVER gets a hand-rolled watcher.
            2. TWO LAYERS: the cheap watcher polling and classifying, and the deep audit team of parallel
               read-only sub-agents on a slower cadence.
            3. FOUR STATES, NOT TWO, and why each needs a different answer (QUESTION to a human, STALLED
               nudged mechanically, BLOCKED never nudged because that is manufactured thrash, WORKING
               silent). The question UI is detected by ONE line carrying BOTH "Enter to select" AND
               "to navigate": either alone fires on ordinary prose.
            4. THE SEVEN DEFECTS, each stated as the invariant plus the false positive that taught it:
               self-echo excluded by content in short slices; one variable per signal; the failure latch
               never cleared on resume; failure STRINGS with punctuation not WORDS ("is RED." not "is
               RED", which matched "is REDundant"; "MISSING ROW:" not "MISSING", which matched the prose
               "missing redirect"); the input box cut structurally not by a tail drop; completed task
               lines dropped before diffing so in-progress transitions are not drowned; and awaiting a
               sign-off IS work, so counting only runnable steps falsely reports BLOCKED.
            5. THE NUDGE BOUND bounds the ABSENCE OF PROGRESS, not the work: reset the counter on every
               advance of the build's own progress metric, stop after N nudges that produced nothing.
               A flat cap stops a healthy long run for no reason. That is what R-LOOP actually wants.
            6. The audit dimensions come from the WATCHED PROJECT's own rules, never a generic checklist,
               because a generic audit finds generic nothing; and auditors are adversarial and state in
               one line when a rule genuinely holds, because an audit that always returns "all clean" is
               an audit nobody reads.
            7. It inherits the whole R-STREAM substrate (rmux not tmux, the absolute rmux path, RMUX not
               \$TMUX, send-keys Enter separate, remote quoting, ~/.ssh/config coordinates, bounded
               probes, the ssh-255 discriminator, injective viewer names, one viewer per target).

          Set kind/category/scopes consistently with R-STREAM (it is an Orchestration rule). Write a
          \`reason\` field in the same register as R-STREAM's: it must say these lessons were each paid
          for by a real false positive, and that false positives train the operator to ignore alerts,
          which is the only thing an alerting system has to lose.

          CRITICAL CO-UPDATES, or the doctor and the test suite go yellow. Find them and update them all:
            - the expected-rule-count / expected-ops constant used by \`crates/omega-core/src/doctor.rs\`
            - any test in rules.rs asserting a count
            - the repo-side markdown export parity if rules.rs has one (grep for how R-STREAM appears
              outside rules.rs and reproduce it)
          Verify with: \`cd ${REPO} && cargo test -p omega-core 2>&1 | tail -20\`. Report actual output.`,
            },
          ]

          phase('Build')
          const results = await pipeline(
            BUILDS,
            b => agent(b.prompt, { label: b.label, phase: 'Build' }),
            (built, b) => agent(
              `You are an ADVERSARIAL verifier. Another agent just built part of the /monitor feature for
          OmegaOS at ${REPO}. Your job is to FALSIFY its claim of success, not to confirm it.

          Read the contract at ${CONTRACT} first, then inspect the ACTUAL FILES ON DISK in this scope:
          ${b.prompt.split('YOUR SCOPE')[1].split('\n\n')[0]}

          The builder reported:
          ${String(built).slice(0, 3000)}

          CHECK, with evidence, and do not take the builder's word for anything:
          1. Do the files actually exist on disk with real content? Read them.
          2. Does it actually build/parse? RUN the real command yourself
             (\`cd ${REPO} && cargo build 2>&1 | tail -20\` for Rust, \`bash -n <file>\` for shell) and
             paste the true output.
          3. Is any contract requirement MISSING or faked? Especially: are all four states really
             distinguished; is the question check really requiring BOTH markers on ONE line; are the
             seven defect fixes really present and not just mentioned in a comment; does the nudge bound
             really reset on progress rather than being a flat cap?
          4. Any placeholder, TODO, stub, or elision left behind?
          5. Any em-dash or en-dash in prose (forbidden, R-NODASH)? Check with
             \`grep -n $'\\u2014\\|\\u2013' <files>\`.

          Report ONLY concrete defects with file:line evidence, most severe first, and a one-line
          verdict of PASS or FAIL. If a requirement genuinely holds, say so in one line: a verifier that
          always says "all clean" is one nobody reads.`,
              { label: `verify:${b.key}`, phase: 'Verify' }
            )
          )

          return { builds: BUILDS.map(b => b.key), verdicts: results }
          )

● Workflow running in background. While it builds, I'll prepare the L1 verification corpus — real pane captures from live sessions, which is the honest way to prove the classifier (real captures, not
  synthetic ones). This touches no repo file:

● Bash(cd /tmp/claude-1000/-home-vibe-Station-SideBusiness-OmegaOS/18c62fa7-dc03-4710-90c8-e68b0d553700/scratchpad
      mkdir -p panes
      for s in AltReality-claude BluePrint-OS WHYOS-claude camelia-claude oracle-OmegaOS; do
        ~/.local/bin/rmux capture-pane -p -t "$s" -S -90 > "panes/$s.txt" 2>/dev/null
        n=$(wc -l < "panes/$s.txt")
        q=$(grep -cE 'Enter to select.*to navigate' "panes/$s.txt")
        w=$(grep -cE 'esc to interrupt|·.*tokens' "panes/$s.txt")
        echo "$s: lines=$n question_line=$q working_marker=$w"
      done)
